evidence_excerpts: The systematic-error section reports a constant reproducible shift of 50 kJ mol^-1 in measured expectation values relative to theoretical energy, attributed to source, circuit, calibration, and coupling effects.
The paper notes that error magnitude increases with R because the first and second excited states become degenerate, making classical minimization harder and increasing estimation variance.
text: Experimental energy estimates are limited by photon-source impurity, photon distinguishability, circuit imperfections, coupling imbalance, and increasing degeneracy-related difficulty at larger bond separations.
